items.text: This characteristic-root method assumes a finite-order recurrence with constant coefficients and a nonzero leading coefficient.
Repeated roots require the polynomial factors in n; merely repeating the same exponential does not create independent solutions.
Complex roots occur in conjugate pairs only when the recurrence coefficients are real.

items.text: Build the characteristic polynomial using a consistent recurrence arrangement; moving terms changes signs.
The number of independent constants must equal the recurrence order, counting root multiplicities.
A closed form derived from roots still needs the initial conditions; characteristic roots alone do not select one sequence.
